div.div: One link cannot tell AP-side from device-side motion; compare links across devices - and add device-to-device links, because links grow as N x N

motion near the AP:
all AP links move together

motion near device 4:
only its links move

Link graph [B4]: blue solid = AP-device links (N); green dashed = device-to-device links via a softAP on each device, same channel as the AP, MAC-filtered. With N = 4 devices [1]: 4 AP links become 16 directed links (N x N, my arithmetic) - and the new links cross rooms the AP links never cross.

Through-wall false positives: motion next door reaches the links through the wall, weakened. Mitigate with more endpoints (the right room responds much more strongly), per-home sensitivity for thin walls, and fusion with a sensor that does not see through walls [B4].
Decision rule: cross-correlate CSI variation across devices [B4]
HIGH correlation across all AP links -> motion near the AP (P): every AP link shares the AP end
LOW correlation, one device's links active -> motion near that device (Q)
Several devices active, LOW mutual correlation -> several people, each near a device

Where: sorted nodes and sorted links [B4]. Node variation w_i = sum_j v_ij; the node with the largest w is probably closest. Take links in order of v; if one end's w is clearly larger (w_i > w_j + T, margin T found empirically), keep the half-plane on that side of the link's perpendicular bisector. The intersection of kept half-planes is the detected area; often the first two or three links decide the room. Equal w at three nodes -> answer "near several nodes". Needs rough device positions.
Same four devices: adding device-to-device links gained more than going from one device to four on AP links. By scenario [3]: near a device 0.95, room with no device 0.6, typing 0.4.

Legend: blue = AP and AP-device links | green = devices, device-to-device links (dashed) | red P, Q = example motions | amber = through-wall caveat | bars: grey 1 device, blue 4 devices AP links, green 4 devices all links. [B4] = kit note; [n] = constants.json entries below.

Numbers (all loaded from constants.json):
[1] home_study_size_illustrative - ILLUSTRATIVE; illustrative shape of a cross-home study; internal I7
[2] devices_tpr_illustrative - ILLUSTRATIVE; illustrative relation: more endpoints help, device-to-device links help more; internal I7
[3] motion_type_tpr_illustrative - ILLUSTRATIVE; illustrative per-scenario spread; internal I7
Notes: [B4] multi-device joint detection (softAP links, cross-correlation rule, sorted nodes/links, through-wall false positives, device-count result); see also [C5] one-device homes. hostapd is open-source.
